text:
nina: quick idea - build a tiny "normalizer" layer to present identical runtime surface across hosted/dedicated/private. focus only on auth claim mapping, telemetry normalization, and capability hints.

leo: is this a network sidecar or an in-process library? both?

nina: both. default is sidecar proxy. provide lib variant for air-gapped installs to avoid hop. runtime reads canonical claims via header or local socket.

carol: main risks: latency (proxy), compatibility drift (private installs), and telemetry/legal redaction.

ben: propose headers: X-RW-Norm-Version and X-RW-Norm-Caps (kv-stable, telemetry-ps). runtime checks caps before enabling cross-request caching.

leo: auth mapping: map local auth -> canonical {tenant, role, req_id, principal}. adapters for mTLS, bearer, signed-kms tokens.

carol: telemetry plugin hook so customers can run redactor before egress. allow wasm/native plugin. default no-op.

nina: config sample: version, fail_mode (closed|open), allow_bypass, caps. default: fail_mode=closed for prod.

infra-bot: ci-bot: created job normalizer-integration-nightly.

ben: rollout: RFC + test harness (hosted sidecar vs lib vs private sidecar), hosted canary, then private pilot. provide strict/lenient version modes.

leo: i'll prototype perf harness. carol you own redaction API doc. nina will write RFC.

nina: thanks all, i'll open ARCH ticket and attach draft RFC.
